title: River flood
summary: Water spreads across farmland and floodplains.
headline: Water inundated 48% of the monitored river basin after heavy monsoon rainfall
whyMatters: Why it matters: Emergency response teams and agricultural coordinators can map inundated crops and isolated villages within hours to deploy relief supplies.
whyRadar: Heavy monsoon clouds completely obscured the disaster zone from optical satellites, but radar signals passed straight through clouds and rain to map surface standing water day and night.
unit: Share of monitored study area inundated by surface water (Sample data)

title: Glacier movement
summary: Ice creeps down a valley and calves into the fjord.
headline: Fast-flowing glacier front advanced 34 meters per day through Ilulissat Icefjord
whyMatters: Why it matters: Glaciologists and climate scientists track polar ice velocity and calving rates to calculate sea level rise contributions and ocean circulation changes.
whyRadar: Polar regions experience months of winter darkness and frequent cloud cover; radar generates its own microwave pulse to detect crevasse displacement and iceberg discharge without daylight.
unit: Glacier flow speed index / relative ice margin displacement (Sample data)

title: Wetland loss
summary: Marshland dries out and vegetative canopy shrinks.
headline: Prolonged drought reduced open marsh surface water by 62% over 3 seasons
whyMatters: Why it matters: Conservationists and water authorities monitor wetland degradation to protect migratory bird sanctuaries, carbon sinks, and underground aquifer health.
whyRadar: Radar backscatter distinguishes between open water, dense reed marsh, and dry soil, and can detect flooded water hidden underneath thick forest and vegetation canopies.
unit: Percentage of wetland basin covered by water and healthy marsh (Sample data)
